edits.old: Replacing Realm is an application migration as well as a data import. PowerSync’s production case changes the local database to SQLite; RxDB’s guide changes schema representation, queries, subscriptions and write APIs. Neither path is a drop-in Realm SDK substitution. (high confidence)
edits.new: Replacing Realm is an application migration as well as a data import. In the Facilitron case, PowerSync replaces Realm's NoSQL client-side database with SQLite on the client, which required some data types to be migrated; RxDB's guide changes schema representation, queries, change listeners (to RxJS subscriptions) and write APIs (from realm.write() to insert/incrementalPatch). Both paths require rewriting application code rather than swapping the Realm SDK. Sources: https://powersync.com/blog/how-facilitron-migrated-from-atlas-device-sync-to-powersync ; https://rxdb.info/articles/realm-to-rxdb-migration.html

evidence.quote: Realm is a NoSQL client-side database, whereas PowerSync uses SQLite on the client-side. This required some data types to be migrated.
Realm Query Language filter strings become Mango query selectors, the same operator style used by MongoDB.
Realm collection and object listeners become RxJS subscriptions.
Realm requires every mutation to happen inside realm.write(). RxDB writes are single document operations that persist immediately.
Each Realm object class becomes one collection with a JSON schema.
